node-1.label: Patient presented with new-onset dizziness while sitting and episodes of near-syncope without loss of consciousness

node-2.label: Patient is a man in his 70s with history of orthotopic heart transplant using biatrial surgical technique, grade 1 cardiac allograft vasculopathy, toxic multinodular goiter status post thyroidectomy, and tremors treated with propranolol

node-3.label: Two weeks prior, his cardiologist measured low blood pressure and stopped amlodipine treatment, after which symptoms improved

node-4.label: At presentation, physical examination showed normotensive blood pressure and unremarkable cardiac examination

why.why: Radiologist and Pathologist analyses both classify medication-related hypotension as a secondary possibility and note it is weakened by the normotensive examination and the competing 4.5-second ventricular pause. Prior low blood pressure on amlodipine and symptom improvement after stopping it still provide some support, but the expert consensus lowers the confidence from 0.45 to 0.30.

Radiologist and Pathologist independently conclude that the 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape and dual sinus node activity directly supports CAV-related arrhythmia and can independently explain the episodic dizziness/near-syncope in this post-transplant patient with grade 1 CAV. Pathologist cautions that missing coronary/IVUS, medication/electrolyte, and biopsy/echo data prevent full exclusion of reversible causes, so the confidence is increased from 0.55 to 0.70 rather than higher.

Radiologist states autonomic dysregulation is less supported, and Pathologist continues to regard it as secondary. Post-transplant cardiac denervation provides a mechanistic basis, but with no autonomic testing available and stronger competing explanations, confidence is decreased from 0.35 to 0.20.

node-9.label: Medication records, serial blood pressure readings, ambulatory monitoring, and autonomic testing results are unavailable

node-10.label: Normotensive examination only refutes persistent hypotension, not episodic episodes

node-14.label: 14-day Zio monitor reveals a 4.5-second ventricular pause with junctional escape and dual sinus node activity

node-16.label: Coronary/IVUS, medication/electrolyte, and biopsy/echo data are missing, preventing full exclusion of reversible causes

node-17.label: Reversible causes of bradyarrhythmia are not fully excluded

attrs.why: Pathologist analysis explicitly states that missing coronary/IVUS, medication/electrolyte, and biopsy/echo data prevent full exclusion of reversible causes, so this remains a diagnostic caveat despite the leading CAV-related arrhythmia hypothesis. Confidence 0.35 reflects that it is a possibility, not a confirmed diagnosis.
